description:
Outcome: Added books survive restart, from owner first-version requirements.
Scope: Built-in filesystem JSON repository for books and next id; single-process serialized atomic mutations; injectable storage; persisted operation ids/results in the same transaction for duplicate-safe retries; bounded request parsing and validation. Loopback binding, configured loopback Host/port allowlist, exact same-origin Origin for mutations, JSON content type and custom same-origin header; reject missing/foreign mutation Origin and foreign supplied read Origin, no permissive CORS. Excludes: loans, UI and accounts.
Acceptance: Acknowledged additions survive restart; ids stay unique. Invalid JSON/fields return 4xx without crashing. Cross-site requests rejected. Only missing data file initializes empty; corruption stops startup without overwriting. Acknowledge only after supported atomic replacement and durability barrier. Pre-replacement failure leaves prior state. When replacement may have occurred but durability confirmation fails, report outcome uncertain, not rollback; stop mutations until recovery reloads/validates disk and reconciles operation id. Startup completes supported durability barrier before accepting mutations. Retried operation cannot duplicate addition.
Behaviour: Explicit empty catalogue and actionable private startup/storage errors; no pupil data in logs/errors. Supported filesystem power-loss limits documented, no unsupported guarantees. Store runtime data under data/.
Verification: node:test HTTP input/Host/Origin/content-type/header rejection tests, temp-directory restart, concurrent writes, corruption, and fault injection before/after replacement with restart and operation-id retry. API clients/tests send required headers. Prerequisites: none. Assumptions: approved single local process and filesystem, dependency-free Node.js.
Setup alias: A1.
title: Durable catalogue and safe HTTP API
